summary.short: South Korea's Public Official Election Act governs presidential, National Assembly and local elections, including campaigns, polls and election media. Article 82-8 bars producing or disseminating realistic AI-generated synthetic content for campaigning from 90 days before election day through election day, and requires labelling of such content at other times.
summary.long: The Act applies to presidential, National Assembly, local council and local government head elections. It sets rules for campaigning, candidate registration, campaign materials, broadcast and online election coverage, public opinion polls and election-management bodies. Article 82-8 prohibits producing, editing, distributing, screening or posting realistic AI-generated audio, images or video for campaigning from 90 days before election day to election day, and requires a label on such material at other times. Article 110 bars false statements of fact about candidates, and Article 82-4 lets election commissions and candidates request deletion of unlawful online content. Pollsters must register, and publication of polls on party support or expected winners is barred from six days before election day. Broadcasters and internet news outlets face fairness duties, with reply rights and commission review. Penalties are cross-referenced; the penalty chapter is not in the fetched text, which is part 1 of 2.

No separate deepfake obligations appear in this part. Target instrument IDs are blank because none of the referenced acts is identified in the registry. Bracketed amendment and Constitutional Court notes are session-law history recorded as text but not coded as events. The amends rows come from the 1994 original act's supplementary provisions and are historical. Supplementary provisions of 2026 (Acts 21577, 21857, 22052) set staggered effective dates that are not coded here.
